subject: FastRetail pilot: TTFT & streaming cadence — success criteria and probe plan
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@fastretail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FastRetail pilot: TTFT & streaming cadence — success criteria and probe plan

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so we stay aligned on the pilot success criteria. Short version up front: FastRetail wants low first-byte latency for conversational flows (TTFT target) plus streaming output for progressive UX; we proposed a short probe to validate that on our Dedicated node with an SSE path and websocket fallback.

Call highlights / requirements you confirmed:
- TTFT targets: goal p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms for typical 20–60 token first-chunk responses.
- Concurrency / throughput: expected steady-state 80–150 rps during peak promotions; burst to 300 rps.
- Streaming: prefer SSE for browser clients; websocket available for mobile app fallback. Chunk cadence preference: 100–250ms per chunk for interactive feel.
- Typical payloads: prompts average ~220 tokens, expected response lengths 40–400 tokens depending on use case (product suggestions vs. personalized rationale).
- Fallbacks: if streaming can't meet p95 TTFT, app will fall back to non-streaming short responses for critical flows.

Proposed probe plan (attached PDF + sample payloads):
1) 1-hour pilot on a dedicated instance with realistic concurrency profile (warm-up 10m, ramp to target over 15m, 30m sustained).
2) Measure TTFT and first-chunk size distribution; instrument with distributed tracing and token timing.
3) Try both SSE and websocket endpoints; validate chunk cadence at 100ms, 200ms, and 350ms pacing.
4) Capture p50/p95/p99 for TTFT, per-chunk latency, and overall completion time; collect logs for KV-cache hit rates.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Samira: confirm the two test accounts we can hit (API key + IP allowlist) and share sample payloads you want included (I attached our sample-payloads.json; please replace with your actuals if different).
- Marcus: can you own the probe config and runbook?
- Aditya: can you prepare SSE/WebSocket endpoints and the short SDK snippet for the FastRetail devs to integrate?

Attachments: fastretail-ttft-probe-plan.pdf, sample-payloads.json, sse-vs-ws-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll queue the runbook once I hear back on the test credentials.

—
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Samira Khan <samira@fastretail.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Leo Park <leo.park@fastretail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 16:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: FastRetail pilot: TTFT & streaming cadence — success criteria and probe plan

Grace —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) TTFT expectations: the consumer-facing product team set a hard goal of p95 <= 300ms for product suggestion flows (most critical). We can tolerate up to 350ms for less-critical rationale messages.
2) Concurrency: 100 rps steady with 250 rps burst is more realistic for our worst-case promo.
3) Chunk cadence: desktop web prefers 120–180ms; mobile app prefers slightly longer cadence (180–300ms) to avoid reflow issues.

We’ll provide the following:
- API key + IP allowlist (I’ll send via secure form).
- A small set of real payloads for product-suggestion and rationale flows (I’ll drop them into the Drive folder you linked).

Also noting we need evidence for compliance: can you include request/response logs for the probe (no PII) and a short statement about KV-cache behavior so our infra team can evaluate cache safety?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with credentials today.

Samira
Head of Platform Integrations, FastRetail
samira@fastretail.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 08:03:45 -0700
Subject: Re: FastRetail pilot: TTFT & streaming cadence — success criteria and probe plan

Grace / Aditya —

I’ll take point on the probe runbook and results capture. Plan below — will publish runbook as a short playbook in the Drive link.

Probe plan (ops playbook highlights):
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated (m5-gpu-a100x1 equivalent) in us-west-2. Configure fixed-quantization model variant that matches what we discussed.
- Workload: use the sample-payloads.json from the Drive; run three cadence passes: 120ms, 200ms, 300ms chunk pacing. For each cadence run: warm-up 10m at 30% target rps, ramp 15m, sustain 30m, cool-down 5m.
- Metrics to capture: TTFT (per-request first-byte timestamp), chunk-emit intervals, per-token CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit ratio, error rates, and tail latencies (p95/p99).
- Concurrency matrix: runs at 50rps, 100rps, 200rps burst tests with 5k total sample requests per config.
- Logging: scrub PII, provide anonymized request/response hashes + timing CSV (latency-probe-results.csv).

Risks / notes:
- SSE generally adds minimal per-connection overhead, but if clients open long-lived SSE with many parallel connections we’ll need to cap total concurrent SSE streams per instance — will document safe thresholds.
- If TTFT p95 is missed due to cold KV cache, we’ll test a priming strategy to pre-warm critical keys during ramp.

I’ll drop the playbook in the Drive folder and schedule the probe once Samira confirms credentials.

—Marcus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastRetail pilot: TTFT & streaming cadence — success criteria and probe plan

Samira —

Perfect, thanks for the fast turnaround. Two quick confirmations before we schedule:
- We will run the first probe tomorrow (Wed 2026-04-29) at 10:00 PT if we receive credentials today by 17:00 PT.
- Deliverables after probe: anonymized latency CSV, trace links, short write-up of findings and recommended cadence + fallback policy (we’ll recommend SSE primary with websocket fallback and a default chunk cadence of 150ms for desktop, 220ms for mobile per your preference).

I’m attaching the PDF probe plan and SSE vs WebSocket decision matrix for your infra team. If anything looks off, reply-all and I’ll update.

Attaching: fastretail-ttft-probe-plan.pdf, sse-vs-ws-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to results.

—
Grace
